# RosmarOps

> RosmarOps reads the configuration of the AI coding agents on your Windows, Linux and macOS (preview) computer (today <!-- agents:scored -->Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cline in VS Code and Gemini CLI<!-- /agents:scored -->) and draws an exposure map: what each agent can read and change, which keys it can reach, and whether one agent can change another agent's configuration or instructions.

Everything is computed on your computer. It sends nothing unless you approve it first, and doesn't change anything on your machine: it only writes its own reports to its own folder. If you choose to paste its export into an AI in the cloud, that text leaves your computer because you paste it.

It runs on Windows and Linux, and on macOS in preview. Today it evaluates <!-- agents:scored -->Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cline in VS Code and Gemini CLI<!-- /agents:scored -->. It detects <!-- agents:detected -->Continue, Antigravity, Claude Desktop and n8n<!-- /agents:detected -->, but doesn't score them yet. Download (Windows): https://github.com/qtorb/rosmarops/releases/latest. Download (Linux): https://rosmarops.com/linux/. Download (macOS, preview): https://rosmarops.com/macos/. How to check it's authentic: https://github.com/qtorb/rosmarops#check-the-download. Source code: https://github.com/qtorb/rosmarops (AGPL-3.0).

- `brew install qtorb/rosmarops/rosmarops` (macOS and Linux, Homebrew)

Can I use it on a work computer? Yes, but tell your security team first. To look for keys, RosmarOps reads the files in your code projects, and some security systems flag many file reads in a short time. It does not open images, documents or other binary files, and it never changes or sends anything without your permission.

## Key terms

- Exposure map: what an agent can do with the permissions it has today. It is not a verdict on whether a machine has been attacked.
- Agent Posture Score: a score out of 100 for each agent, calculated with a versioned formula; when the formula changes, the report says so.
- What wasn't read doesn't count as clean.

- [AI agent map: what each one can do without asking you](https://rosmarops.com/observatory/ai-agent-map/): each scored agent's default class from A to D, its six axes and its factory score, from the engine's data at each release

- [Kanvas on Windows: what it leaves on your computer](https://rosmarops.com/observatory/kanvas/): observatory page, with its data at https://rosmarops.com/observatory/kanvas.json
- [What is an AI agent orchestrator?](https://rosmarops.com/agent-orchestrators/): An AI agent orchestrator is a program that launches several AI agents at once, such as Claude Code or Codex, and hands each one part of the work.
- [What can Claude Code subagents do without asking you?](https://rosmarops.com/claude-code-subagents/): A Claude Code subagent can do whatever the header of its file allows: if the header lists no tools, it inherits every tool of the conversation, and it can have its own permission mode, its own commands and its own MCP servers.
- [What is an MCP server, and why does it give an AI agent power?](https://rosmarops.com/mcp-servers/): An MCP server gives an AI agent a new tool, such as reading your email or writing to your repository, and the agent can then do everything that server's key allows.
- [Videos](https://rosmarops.com/videos/): short videos about AI agents, in Spanish with an AI-generated presenter.
- [Paperclip: an AI agent company, with limits](https://rosmarops.com/videos/paperclip-ai-agent-company/): Paperclip gives you a company of agents, but by default it puts no limits on them. You set those limits.
- [A worktree is not a sandbox](https://rosmarops.com/videos/a-worktree-is-not-a-sandbox/): A worktree keeps the files apart, not the access. To keep the access apart, the sandbox in every agent.
